title: Finite coefficient model of a principal-open cover
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, n,c natural numbers, and f_i in R[x_1,...,x_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let R₀ be a finite type integer subring of R [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with polynomials f₀,i mapping to f_i. Let ι be any type and G_j polynomials over R₀. Suppose every prime of S=R[x]/(f_i) avoids the image of some G_j [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exist a subring R₁ of R containing R₀ and finite type over ℤ, such that every prime of S₁=R₁[x]/(map(R₀→R₁)(f₀,i)) avoids map(R₀→R₁)(G_j) for some j. No fibre-dimension hypothesis or conclusion is included. The indexing type may be empty and both quotient rings may be zero.

proof.text: By the basic-open/unit-ideal criterion the images g_j generate 1 in S. Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite gives a finite subset J of their image generating 1. Choose an index j(x) for each x in J. Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun gives coefficients b_x with sum b_x x=1. Lift b_x through the quotient map to polynomials H_x. The polynomial t=1-sum H_x map(G_j(x)) maps to zero, hence belongs to the equation ideal. Express t=sum a_i f_i by the finite-span membership criterion. For an empty cover J may be empty and the same identity gives 1 in the equation ideal.

Let C be the finite union of the coefficient sets of a_i and H_x, and construct R₁ as the underlying subring of Algebra.adjoin R₀ C in R. It contains the image of R₀ by the algebra-map membership property. Algebra.FiniteType.adjoin_of_finite and transitivity prove finite type over ℤ. The other polynomials already have coefficients in R₀; their maps therefore lie over R₁. Lift a_i and H_x using MvPolynomial.mem_range_map_iff_coeffs_subset. Their lifts are uniquely determined because R₁→R is injective.

Injectivity of the coefficient map on multivariate polynomials transports sum a₁,i f₁,i=1-sum H₁,x G₁,x to R₁[x]. Apply the quotient map: the equation terms vanish, so sum bar(H₁,x) bar(G₁,x)=1. If every G_j belonged to a given prime, its closure under polynomial multiplication and finite sums would put 1 in it, contradicting properness. This proves the descended cover.
